focus: Practical software engineering, scientific research tools, and automation across sectors
title: Reading Images by Their Frequencies
utility_use_case: A microscopy team is preparing a large image archive for transfer to a collaborator. Before choosing a retention or packaging plan, an engineer runs `bash duplicate-report.sh --root ./assets` to identify byte-identical image files and estimate storage that might be redundant. The JSON output gives paths, file sizes, shared SHA-256 digests, and a potential byte total. The team can investigate whether duplicates are intentional, then make any archive changes through its normal reviewed process. The utility itself only reports and never deletes.

source.section_title: Chapter 6: Fourier Transform in Image Processing

editorial_review.summary: Qualified the convolution theorem for finite DFTs, clarified which symlinks and path components are skipped, and included per-file hashing overhead in the complexity description.

edits.old: The convolution theorem explains why frequency methods are connected to familiar spatial filters: spatial convolution corresponds to multiplication in the frequency domain, and spatial multiplication corresponds to convolution in frequency.
edits.new: The convolution theorem explains why frequency methods are connected to familiar spatial filters: for a finite DFT, circular spatial convolution corresponds to coefficient-wise multiplication in frequency, while spatial multiplication corresponds, up to normalization, to circular convolution in frequency. Linear convolution requires suitable padding.

edits.old: Symbolic links and paths with any hidden component, meaning a path part beginning with `.`, are skipped.
edits.new: Symbolic links beneath the root and paths with any hidden component, meaning a relative path part beginning with `.`, are skipped.

edits.old: Hashing takes time proportional to $B$, with additional traversal, sorting, and bookkeeping costs.
edits.new: Hashing takes time proportional to $B$, plus per-file overhead, with additional traversal, sorting, and bookkeeping costs.
